motion.purpose: Directional wind on the wheat, never a circular orbit. Seam-safe across tiles; sky static. Animates on the index; an article reading view renders one static frame so nothing moves while reading; same static frame under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview: moving forward is a personal field journal, and the design treats the page as the calm printout of the same generator that draws its background. A generated ASCII wheat field animates along the bottom of every screen, swaying like wind, and the writing sits above it as a spare monospace manifest: a section label with a dotted leader, then aligned rows of date, title, tag, and a reading-length meter drawn from the field's own glyph ramp. The masthead is modest, not a billboard, so the index of posts comes up almost immediately. The generated character is carried honestly: a comment-style provenance line near the masthead and a footer build stamp both print the field's real parameters injected at build time. Structure reads as program output: routes in the nav, dotted plotter rules instead of solid borders, a translucent paper wash so the field keeps breathing in the margins. Density stays low; type is one weight, color is soft, motion is ambient and directional.
keyCharacteristics: Animated ASCII wheat field as the only ornament, fixed behind a translucent reading sheet that lets it show through the margins.
The post index is a generated manifest: aligned date / title / tag / read columns, the read column a meter built from the field's glyph ramp.
Honest provenance: masthead comment and footer build stamp print real, generator-injected values.
Monospace carries all chrome and the index; long-form article bodies use a warm reading serif. Hierarchy from size and a 400/500 split, never bold. Modest masthead.
Dotted hairline rules (the plotter/printout texture); zero shadows, zero corner radius.
Articles open in a calm reading mode: serif body on a feathered paper-wash halo, the field held still.

rules.name: The Field-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Wheat color lives in the backdrop field and the reading meter only. Never use a wheat tone as a chrome accent, fill, or text color.

rules.name: The Soft-Ink Rule
rules.body: Body is #3a342b, headings #27221b, secondary #6b6253 (AA ~6:1). Pure black (#000) is prohibited.

rules.name: The Mono-Chrome, Serif-Reading Rule
rules.body: Monospace carries all chrome, labels, the manifest, the masthead, and every article heading. The only second typeface is the reading serif, in long-form article body copy alone. Contrast in mono is size plus the 400/500 split, never bold.

rules.name: The Reading-Width Rule
rules.body: Monospace prose (lede, About) caps near 56 to 60ch; the serif article body caps near 65 to 70ch (a ~40rem column). The manifest table runs wider inside the 720px column because tabular rows need the room.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Box-shadows are prohibited as decoration. The only lift is the header's backdrop blur.

rules.name: The Flat-Edge Rule
rules.body: Corner radius is 0 everywhere. No rounded cards, pills, or softened inputs.

rules.name: The Dotted-Rule Rule
rules.body: Structural rules are 1px dotted at Ink/16%, never solid. The dotted texture is the printout signature.

rules.name: The Paper-Wash Rule
rules.body: Conceal the field with a soft white wash wherever sustained reading sits, never a hard-edged panel. The wash feathers into the field at its margins (a horizontal white-to-transparent gradient, the veil rotated); on an article reading view the field stops animating. A gradient that reveals the background is atmosphere, not elevation.

rules.name: The Quiet-and-Hand-Built Rule
rules.body: Chrome should feel quiet and hand-built. If a piece draws attention to itself, it is wrong; the writing and the field are the subjects.

rules.name: The Generated-Provenance Rule
rules.body: Provenance and build stamps print the shared field payload's real parameters (source name, grid size, color count, generated date), never hardcoded or invented.

rules.name: The Manifest-Index Rule
rules.body: Post lists render as aligned generated indices keyed on the ISO date column. Never reintroduce 01 / 02 / 03 numbered section markers.

dos: Do keep body in Ink (#3a342b), headings in Ink Strong (#27221b), secondary in Ink Muted (#6b6253, AA).
Do use dotted hairlines (#2a221629) for every rule, nothing solid or heavier.
Do set chrome, labels, the manifest, and article headings in the one monospace family at weight 400 (500 for small labels); reserve the reading serif for long-form article bodies.
Do render post lists as aligned manifests keyed on the ISO date, in semantic <ul> lists with <h2> section headings.
Do keep the reading sheet translucent and feather its edges so the field breathes instead of meeting a hard cut.
Do keep decorative glyphs (meter, cursor, stamps) aria-hidden, and give interactive rows a visible :focus-visible state matching hover.
Do print real generator values in the provenance and build stamps.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion with the static field frame.
Do edit tools/page_template.html, tools/post_template.html, or field-renderer.js, then rebuild; never hand-edit generated index.html, post.html, or field-data.js.
Do set long-form article body copy in the reading serif, and freeze the field on an article reading view so nothing moves while reading.
donts: Don't build busy SaaS landing pages: no hero-metric template, dense card grids, or stacked calls to action.
Don't fall into the generic dev-blog template look: no default sans, boxed cards, or sidebar clutter.
Don't add loud motion: no scroll-jacking, parallax spectacle, per-section entrance animation, or circular/orbiting field motion.
Don't reach for corporate gloss: no navy-and-gradient sterility or stock polish.
Don't ship anything that reads as AI-generated or templated.
Don't use pure black (#000), drop shadows, corner radius, solid heavy borders, or a bold display weight. The reading serif is the only permitted second typeface, body-only.
Don't use a wheat tone as a chrome accent or text color, and don't reintroduce 01 / 02 / 03 numbered markers.
Don't set article headings, the title, or the masthead in serif, or add an italic display serif or drop caps: that tips into the saturated editorial-typographic lane.
